extracted.intended_audience: Researchers/authors preparing manuscripts for the Bulletin of Symbolic Logic (Association for Symbolic Logic)
extracted.subtask_short: submitting to Bulletin of Symbolic Logic
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for authors preparing and submitting manuscripts to the Bulletin of Symbolic Logic, including what kinds of contributions the journal publishes, expectations for accessibility and scope, and procedural notes about submission and open-access charges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The Bulletin of Symbolic Logic was established in 1995 by the Association for Symbolic Logic to provide a journal of high standards that would be both accessible and of interest to as wide an audience as possible. It is designed to cover all areas within the purview of the ASL: mathematical logic and its applications, philosophical and non-classical logic and its applications, history and philosophy of logic, and philosophy and methodology of mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions should fall within these topical areas and aim for high standards while remaining accessible to a broad audience of logicians and related scholars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary article types: Articles
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles presenting topics of broad interest in a way that is accessible to a large audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An Article should treat a topic of broad interest and be written so that a wide readership of logicians can follow; emphasis on accessibility and broad appeal within the ASL community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary article types: Communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Communications which are announcements of important new results and ideas in any aspect of logic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communications are intended for announcing important new results and ideas; they differ from Articles in being focused announcements rather than broad expository treatments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other published items
rubrics_metrics.description: The Bulletin also publishes a Reviews Section, a Thesis Abstract Section and reports of ASL meetings, Notices of interest to logicians, and the annual listing of ASL officers, Council members, committee members, and individual and institutional members of the Association.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors proposing book reviews, thesis abstracts, meeting reports, or notices should follow the appropriate section conventions (links to specific sections/pages are implied).

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission system account requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: You will need an account for the submission system, which is separate to your Cambridge Core account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the partner submission system; for login and submission support, visit the submission and support pages. Click 'Proceed to submission system' to continue to the partner's website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare your materials before submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Please review this journal's author instructions, particularly the preparing your materials page, before submitting your manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are explicitly directed to consult the 'preparing your materials' guidance prior to submission — this likely contains formatting, file, and metadata requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open access / APC eligibility note
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain article types (for example, Research Articles and Surveys) may be eligible for APC waivers or discounts under one of the agreements Cambridge University Press has made to support open access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For accepted Articles or Communications published Gold Open Access, all or part of the publication costs may be covered by agreements; authors should check eligibility and applicable agreements.
